Description: This proposed research aims to develop a statistical inference and modeling framework for characterizing the DYNAMIC stability and performance of blunt-body systems. we define hybrid analysis and modeling (ham) AS our holistic approach to the complementary integration of principled physics-based and data-driven models. designing a reinforcement learning (rl) suite, we will explore the feasibility of new learning approaches to elucidate new physical insights in characterizing vehicle stability and identify the effect of information density on various aspects of multimodal resources extracted from experiments and high-fidelity simulations. within this framework, we propose to develop a physics-guided multifidelity learning (pgml) approach to statistically infer DYNAMIC stability parameters in modeling free-flight behavior with reduced uncertainty. our pgml design is therefore motivated to provide a trustworthy learning platform with enhanced model fusion capabilities BY incorporating physics-based or rule-based functional concatenation layers and inductive biases. we will enhance our hybrid ham-rl (hrl) suite with feature engineering and symbolic regression capabilities in our effort toward forging explainable learning platforms. like in many other fields, we are steadily moving away from sparse data to rich data regimes in space science, thanks to rapid advances in the diagnostic, manufacturing and computing technologies in recent years. we highlight that this growth has resulted in two major challenges. FIRST, the data exhibits a high correlation in many systems, which implies more data does not necessarily translate into more information. second, it is computationally demanding to train an end-to-end data-driven model that CAN be trustworthily used in future predictions. consequently, our hybrid data-driven approach offers a holistic solution to address both challenges seamlessly. specifically, the continuous increase in the 4v's (i.e., volume, velocity, variety, and veracity) of data generated in planetary entry aerodynamics coupled with growing demands for accurate computational methodologies for NASA's martian and DAVINCI missions have prompted the need for novel theory-guided data-driven technologies with improved predictive performance, uncertainty quantification, validation and verification characteristics. it is evident that computational modeling plays a vital role in enhancing the capability of integrated system tools (e.g., digital twins) of planetary entry vehicles. hence, any data-driven modeling approach should at least be generalizable, trustworthy, efficient, accurate, and self-adapting. in this research, we therefore propose to take a novel interdisciplinary approach to these challenges BY designing a domain-specific ham framework. our approach to aerodynamic modeling, data collection, and data reduction will respond to generating a multifidelity model fusion capability that synthesizes heterogeneous multimodal experimental and simulation datasets. ham offers a modular platform to embed existing theoretical models, curve fits, and look-up tables seamlessly to accelerate the analysis, design, and development of Entry, Descent, and Landing technologies. designing these ham models and inference tools (to be integrated in our proposed hrl suite) that provide diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive capabilities to the vehicle and mission design operations could therefore revolutionize the development of planetary entry systems.
